slides.say: Kobi bought a pair of pants at a fifty percent discount, and a shirt at a ten percent discount. He paid two hundred eighty shekels in total, instead of five hundred shekels. What was the price of the shirt before the discount?
at: Kobi bought a pair of pants

slides.say: If we solve it the math way, we need two unknowns and two equations, and few students really manage that. But we have answers. The choices are numbers, and the story gives conditions we can check. So we look for the choice that fits everything in the story when we plug it in.
We haven't learned percents yet, so here's all we need. Fifty percent off means half the price is taken off, so he pays half. Ten percent off means a tenth of the price is taken off.
And one more thing from the story. Before the discounts, the pants and the shirt cost five hundred together. So once we know the shirt, the pants are five hundred minus the shirt.
at: the pants are five hundred minus

slides.say: Which choice first? The round, convenient ones, fifty and a hundred fifty. Let's try fifty. If the shirt cost fifty, the pants cost five hundred minus fifty, four hundred fifty.
at: the pants cost five hundred minus fifty

slides.say: The pants are half price, so he paid half of four hundred fifty, two hundred twenty-five. On the shirt, a tenth of fifty is five, so he paid fifty minus five, forty-five.
at: he paid half of four hundred fifty
a tenth of fifty is five

slides.say: Together, two hundred twenty-five plus forty-five is two hundred seventy. But he paid two hundred eighty, so choice number one is out.
at: so choice number one is out

slides.say: I'm a little disappointed. I tried a round answer and it didn't work. But that's fine, we go on. The next round one is a hundred fifty. Then the pants are five hundred minus a hundred fifty, three hundred fifty.
at: Then the pants are five hundred minus

slides.say: Half of three hundred fifty is a hundred seventy-five. A tenth of a hundred fifty is fifteen, so the shirt cost him a hundred fifty minus fifteen, a hundred thirty-five.
at: A tenth of a hundred fifty

slides.say: Together, a hundred seventy-five plus a hundred thirty-five is three hundred ten. That's not two hundred eighty either, so choice number four is out too.
at: so choice number four is out too

slides.say: What's going on here? We said the right answer is usually one of the round ones, and here it isn't. Usually doesn't mean always. This question is here exactly so we learn what to do when it doesn't work out. And what do we do? We just go on as usual.
Two choices are left, seventy-five and a hundred forty. We try the rounder one, a hundred forty. Then the pants are five hundred minus a hundred forty, three hundred sixty.

Half of three hundred sixty is a hundred eighty. A tenth of a hundred forty is fourteen, so the shirt cost him a hundred forty minus fourteen, a hundred twenty-six. Together, a hundred eighty plus a hundred twenty-six is three hundred six. Not two hundred eighty, so choice number three is out.
at: A tenth of a hundred forty
so choice number three is out

slides.say: Now only choice number two is left. Can I mark it without checking? Yes. Three choices are out, so the one that's left must be right. Choice number two is our answer, seventy-five.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: Let's go back to the moment we had tried the two round answers. We could have saved a step there with an estimate.
at: Let's go back to the moment

slides.say: A shirt of fifty gave two hundred seventy, and a shirt of a hundred fifty gave three hundred ten. We need two hundred eighty, which is between them. So the shirt is between fifty and a hundred fifty.

And two hundred eighty is much closer to two hundred seventy than to three hundred ten. It's ten away from one, and thirty away from the other. So the shirt is much closer to fifty than to a hundred fifty.
at: much closer to two hundred seventy
So the shirt is much closer

slides.say: Of the two choices left, seventy-five is close to fifty, and a hundred forty is right next to a hundred fifty. So the answer is seventy-five.

slides: If you saw that, great. If not, no problem. We plugged in one more answer and crossed it out. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
